newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss November central bank money rises 5.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss November central bank money rises 5.0 pct.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) said seasonally-adjusted central bank money supply rose by around 1.5 billion Swiss francs in November to 31.760 billion for an increase of 5.0 percent compared with the 1995 fourth quarter.

The SNB said in an advance release of its December monthly report that sight deposits on average rose 115 million francs in November to 3.290 billion and notes in circulation had risen 3.0 percent to 28.152 billion.
The 5.0 percent rise in November money supply compares with with the SNB's recent forecast for a 4.5 percent expansion in the fourth quarter this year from the same 1995 period.

At its semi-annual news conference on December 13, the SNB said it would continue to be generous with liquidity in light of the unfavourable economic climate and uncertainties around the evolution of Europe's single currency.
